34193-the-true-benjamin-franklin.title: Benjamin Franklin
34193-the-true-benjamin-franklin.creator: Sydney George Fisher
34193-the-true-benjamin-franklin.description: A book by Sydney George Fisher. Painted, as is supposed, in London in 1726, when he was twenty  years old, and now in the possession of Harvard University. Its  history and the doubts as to its authenticity are given in the  text.

arxiv-2203-01532.title: Exploring Patch-wise Semantic Relation for Contrastive Learning in Image-to-Image Translation Tasks
arxiv-2203-01532.creator: Chanyong Jung, Gihyun Kwon, Jong Chul Ye, Department of Bio, Brain Engineering, Graduate School of AI, KAIST {jcy132, cyclomon , jong.ye}@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2203-01532.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chanyong Jung, Gihyun Kwon, Jong Chul Ye, Department of Bio, Brain Engineering, Graduate School of AI, KAIST {jcy132, cyclomon , jong.ye}@kaist.ac.kr. Recently, contrastive learning-based image translation methods have been proposed, which contrasts different spatial locations to enhance the spatial correspondence. However, the methods often ignore the diverse semantic relation within the images.

arxiv-2204-11956.title: Spontaneous Emergence of Computation in Network Cascades
arxiv-2204-11956.creator: Galen J. Wilkerson, Sotiris Moschoyiannis, Henrik Jeldtoft Jensen
arxiv-2204-11956.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Galen J. Wilkerson, Sotiris Moschoyiannis, Henrik Jeldtoft Jensen. Neuronal network computation and computation by avalanche supporting networks are of interest to the fields of physics, computer science (computation theory as well as statistical or machine learning) and neuroscience. Here we show that computation of complex Boolean functions arises spontaneously in threshold networks as a function of connectivity and antagonism (inhibition), computed by logic automata (motifs) in the form of computational cascades .

arxiv-2206-02855.title: Efficient entity-based reinforcement learning
arxiv-2206-02855.creator: Vince Jankovics, Michael Garcia Ortiz, Eduardo Alonso
arxiv-2206-02855.description: Abstract Recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) successes rely on end-to-end learning from fixed-size observational inputs (e.g. image, state-variables). However, many challenging and interesting problems in decision making involve observations or intermediary representations which are best described as a set of entities: either the image-based approach would miss small but important details in the observations (e.g.

arxiv-2211-08691.title: Towards Long-Tailed 3D Detection
arxiv-2211-08691.creator: Neehar Peri, Achal Dave, Deva Ramanan, Shu Kong
arxiv-2211-08691.description: Abstract Contemporary autonomous vehicle (AV) benchmarks have advanced techniques for training 3D detectors, particularly on large-scale LiDAR data. Surprisingly, although semantic class labels naturally follow a long-tailed distribution, these benchmarks focus on only a few common classes (e.g., pedestrian and car ) and neglect many rare classes in-the-tail (e.g., debris and stroller ).

arxiv-2211-09454.title: DeepPrivacy2: Towards Realistic Full-Body Anonymization
arxiv-2211-09454.creator: Håkon Hukkelås Frank Lindseth Norwegian University of Science and Technology hakon.hukkelas@ntnu.no
arxiv-2211-09454.description: Abstract Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are widely adopted for anonymization of human figures. However, current state-of-the-art limits anonymization to the task of face anonymization. In this paper, we propose a novel anonymization framework (DeepPrivacy2) for realistic anonymization of human figures and faces.

arxiv-2212-08708.title: Testing the Radio-Selection Method of Dual Active Galactic Nuclei in the Stripe 82 Field
arxiv-2212-08708.creator: Arran C. Gross, Hai Fu, A. D. Myers, S. G. Djorgovski, Joshua L. Steffen, and J. M. Wrobel
arxiv-2212-08708.description: Abstract We test the merger-induced dual active galactic nuclei (dAGN) paradigm using a sample of 35 radio galaxy pairs from the SDSS Stripe 82 field. Using Keck optical spectroscopy, we confirm 21 pairs have consistent redshifts, constituting kinematic pairs; the remaining 14 pairs are line-of-sight projections.

arxiv-2405-03097.title: To Each (Textual Sequence) Its Own: Improving Memorized-Data Unlearning in Large Language Models
arxiv-2405-03097.creator: George-Octavian Bărbulescu, Peter Triantafillou
arxiv-2405-03097.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by George-Octavian Bărbulescu, Peter Triantafillou. LLMs have been found to memorize training textual sequences and regurgitate verbatim said sequences during text generation time. This fact is known to be the cause of privacy and related (e.g., copyright) problems. Unlearning in LLMs then takes the form of devising new algorithms that will properly deal with these side-effects of memorized data, while not hurting the model’s utility.

arxiv-2409-18310.title: A Survey of Simplicial, Relative, and Chain Complex Homology Theories for Hypergraphs
arxiv-2409-18310.creator: Ellen Gasparovic, Emilie Purvine, Radmila Sazdanovic, Bei Wang, Yusu Wang, Lori Ziegelmeier
arxiv-2409-18310.description: Abstract . Hypergraphs have seen widespread application in network and data science communities in recent years. We present a survey of recent work to construct auxiliary structures from hypergraphs—specifically simplicial, relative, and chain complexes—that can be used to build homology theories for hypergraphs. We define and describe nine different constructions and their associated homology theories.

arxiv-2412-02656.title: Geometric bound on structure factor
arxiv-2412-02656.creator: Yugo Onishi, Alexander Avdoshkin, Liang Fu
arxiv-2412-02656.description: Abstract We show that a quadratic form of quantum geometric tensor in k k -space sets a bound on the q 4 q^{4} term in the static structure factor S ⁡ ( q ) S(q) at small 𝒒 {\bf\it q} .

arxiv-2506-13281.title: EPC Framework for BESS Projects
arxiv-2506-13281.creator: Zeenat Hameed, Chresten Træholt
arxiv-2506-13281.description: Abstract Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are critical for modern power networks, supporting grid services such as frequency regulation, peak shaving, and black‐start. Delivering a BESS under an Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) model requires a concise methodology that balances regulatory compliance, technical details, and schedule efficiency.

arxiv-2506-22605.title: Goodness-of-fit Tests for Combined Unilateral and Bilateral Data
arxiv-2506-22605.creator: Jia Zhou, Chang-Xing Ma
arxiv-2506-22605.description: Abstract Clinical trials involving paired organs often yield a mixture of unilateral and bilateral data, where each subject may contribute either one or two responses under certain circumstances. While unilateral responses from different individuals can be treated as independent, bilateral responses from the same individual are likely correlated.

arxiv-2507-12445.title: CRAFT: Laten c y and Cost-Awa r e Genetic-Based Framework for Node Pl a cement in Edge- F og Environmen t s
arxiv-2507-12445.creator: Soheil Mahdizadeh, Amir Mahdi Rasouli, Mohammad Pourashory, Sadra Galavani, Mohsen Ansari
arxiv-2507-12445.description: Abstract Reducing latency in the Internet of Things (IoT) is a critical concern. While cloud computing facilitates communication, it falls short of meeting real-time requirements reliably. Edge and fog computing have emerged as viable solutions by positioning computing nodes closer to end users, offering lower latency and increased processing power.

arxiv-2511-11382.title: Self-gravitating baryonic tubes supported by π \pi - and ω \omega -mesons and its flat limit
arxiv-2511-11382.creator: Gonzalo Barriga, Carla Henríquez Baez, Leonardo Sanhueza, Aldo Vera
arxiv-2511-11382.description: Abstract In this paper, we construct self-gravitating topological solitons in the S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) Einstein non-linear sigma model coupled to ω \omega -vector-mesons in D = 4 D=4 space-time dimensions. These solutions represent tube-like configurations free of curvature singularities and possess a non-vanishing topological charge identified as the baryon number.

arxiv-2601-21424.title: Lossy Common Information in a Learnable Gray-Wyner Network
arxiv-2601-21424.creator: Anderson de Andrade, Alon Harell & Ivan V. Bajić
arxiv-2601-21424.description: Abstract Many computer vision tasks share substantial overlapping information, yet conventional codecs tend to ignore this, leading to redundant and inefficient representations. The Gray-Wyner network, a classical concept from information theory, offers a principled framework for separating common and task-specific information.

plos-pone-0010940.description: PLOS ONE research article. The emergence of resistant HIV strains, together with the severe side-effects of existing drugs and lack of development of effective anti-HIV vaccines highlight the need for novel antivirals, as well as innovative methods to facilitate their discovery. Here, we have developed an

pmc-10648521.title: Quantitative Study on the Breast Density and the Volume of the Mammary Gland According to the Patient’s Age and Breast Quadrant
pmc-10648521.creator: Sojin Shim, Jan Unkelbach, Anna Landsmann, Andreas Boss
pmc-10648521.description: Objectives: Breast density is considered an independent risk factor for the development of breast cancer. This study aimed to quantitatively assess the percent breast density (PBD) and the mammary glands volume (MGV) according to the patient’s age and breast quadrant. We propose a regression model to estimate PBD and MGV as a function of the patient’s age.

pmc-10717122.title: Elevated serum neuropeptide Y levels are associated with carotid plaque formation in Chinese adults: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10717122.creator: Wan-da Wang, Hui-li Lin, Yan-li Zheng, Sheng-nan Wang, Yao-guo Wang
pmc-10717122.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundCarotid plaque (CP) formation is an important consequence of atherosclerosis and leads to significant complications. Levels of neuropeptide Y (NPY), which is a sympathetic neurotransmitter, are elevated in cardiovascular diseases. It also has important roles in inflammatory conditions.

pmc-10744878.title: A Case of Polymyositis Associated with Cytomegalovirus Infection in a Patient with Hashimoto’s Thyroiditis
pmc-10744878.creator: Ergeta Ktona, Blerta Budani, Ioannis Kostas-Agnantis, Alma Idrizi
pmc-10744878.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Polymyositis is a rare condition with an unknown etiology occurring more frequently in adult women. There is a lack of evidence on the coexistence of PM and CMV infection in a patient with hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto’s Thyroiditis. However, the growing occurrence of both CMV infection and the simultaneous occurrence of autoimmune diseases points out a relationship, while the association direction remains unclear.

pmc-12623586.title: Real-World 24-Month Outcomes of Ofatumumab in Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis: Efficacy, Safety, and the Impact of Frailty
pmc-12623586.creator: Gina Ferrazzano, Roberta Fantozzi, Shalom Haggiag, Doriana Landi, Francesca Napoli, Maria Chiara Buscarinu, Leonardo Malimpensa, Assunta Bianco, Giovanna Borriello, Elena Barbuti, Fabiana Marinelli, Fabrizia Monteleone, Francesca Marchione, Nicola Falcone, Marta Altieri, Giorgio Leodori, Daniele Bel
pmc-12623586.description: IntroductionOfatumumab (OFA) is a highly effective therapeutic option for multiple sclerosis (MS), but real-world data on its efficacy and safety remain limited. We evaluated the real-world efficacy and safety of OFA in patients with MS and explored the predictive value of frailty.

pmc-12641151.title: Prevalence and Predictors of Cognitive Decline Among Diabetes Mellitus Patients Attending Jinja Regional Referral Hospital: A Cross‐Sectional Study in Eastern Uganda
pmc-12641151.creator: Jasper Silver Makasi, Narayana Goruntla, Bhavana Reddy Bommireddy, Bhavani Mopuri, Easwaran Vigneshwaran, Mohammad Jaffar Sadiq Mantargi, Vishnuvandana Bandaru, Joseph Obiezu Chukwujekwu Ezeonwumelu, Tadele Mekuriya Yadesa
pmc-12641151.description: Background and AimsThe burden of cognitive impairment (CI) is high in diabetes mellitus. CI can adversely affect the self‐care and management of diabetes, which results in an increase in the risk of hypo‐ or hyperglycaemic events and diabetic complications. The study aimed to determine the prevalence and predictors of CI in diabetic patients.

pmc-12670102.title: Resurgence of multistate cholera in Sudan amidst ongoing conflict
pmc-12670102.creator: Ayman Azhary, Nooh Mohamed Hajhamed, Rana Mohamed, Eman Taha Osman Ali, Mohammed Elfatih Hamida, Claude Mambo Muvunyi, Emmanuel Edwar Siddig
pmc-12670102.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highlights•Cholera cases surged in Sudan, peaking at 50,832 in 2024 amid conflict.•The Red Sea state reported the highest case fatality rate of 3% in 2023’s cholera outbreak.•Ongoing surveillance and targeted interventions are crucial for outbreak control.Keywords: Cholera outbreaks, Changing trends, Sudan, Case fatality rates (CFRs)

Introduction

Cholera, a waterborne illness caused by Vibrio cholerae, remains a significant public health threat in developing countries due to poor access to drinking water, sanitation, hygiene, armed conflict, and climate change.

pmc-13122071.title: Artificial intelligence-based lung nodule detection for pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas on chest computed tomography
pmc-13122071.creator: Kimei Azama, Nanae Tsuchiya, Shun Toyosato, Koji Yonemoto, Akihiro Nishie
pmc-13122071.description: BACKGROUNDPulmonary arteriovenous fistulas (PAVFs) are abnormal vascular communications between pulmonary arteries and veins that may cause hypoxemia and paradoxical embolism. Because many patients are asymptomatic, PAVFs are often detected incidentally on chest computed tomography (CT). Accurate identification of PAVFs is clinically important for appropriate management; however, small or atypical lesions may be overlooked during routine interpretation.

pmc-13263569.title: A bone graft substitute is effective for posterior spinal fusion in patients with juvenile or adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a retrospective study
pmc-13263569.creator: Conner J Paez, Alexandria N Rundell, Richard P Steiner, Todd F Ritzman, Lorena V Floccari
pmc-13263569.description: BackgroundBone grafting is used to achieve fusion during surgical treatment of scoliosis. While both iliac crest autografts and allografts are effective options, each has associated risks. Synthetic alternatives without added biologics may achieve fusion while reducing or avoiding many of the risks associated with other bone graft options.

pmc-13265981.title: A case of lung nodular aspergilloma mimicking tumor metastasis accompanied by pulmonary embolism in a gastric cancer patient in remission
pmc-13265981.creator: Ali Osman Kaya, Aysun Kaya, Cemal Gundogdu
pmc-13265981.description: Lung aspergilloma is a noninvasive form of fungal infection of the Aspergillus species and usually presents radiologically as nodular masses in the lungs of patients with pulmonary tuberculosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and immunosuppressed patients. It may mimic lung metastatic nodules or primary lung cancer.

pmc-13335253.title: Bundibugyo virus detection during an Ebola virus disease outbreak in the democratic Republic of the Congo: an urgent call for action
pmc-13335253.creator: Christian Tague, Johan Domga, Josias Silatchom Kamgang, Berthol Fotsing Tawe, Hermann Yokolo, Stephane Hans Bateyi
pmc-13335253.description: Ebola virus disease continues to pose a major public health threat in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with outbreaks caused by different Ebola virus species, including Bundibugyo virus. We report preliminary information from an ongoing outbreak investigation based on laboratory testing conducted by the National Institute of Biomedical Research.

pmc-13438123.title: A Test of the Cognitive Benefits of Bilingualism With the Early Childhood Inhibitory Touchscreen Task
pmc-13438123.creator: Alexandra Piuze, Sayde Jennings, Diane Poulin‐Dubois
pmc-13438123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). There is some evidence suggesting that bilingual children differ from monolingual children in cognitive processing due to their exposure to a more complex environment. While several studies have supported this hypothesis, most research has focused on school‐age children. The present study examined whether differences in inhibitory control between monolinguals and bilinguals are present early in life with the Early Childhood Inhibitory Touchscreen Task (ECITT).
